This paper compares six score aggregation strategies—maximum, mean, product, Dempster-Shafer combination, learned linear combination, and a voting threshold rule—for combining per-protocol anomaly scores from Modbus, DNP3, and EtherNet/IP detectors deployed simultaneously on the same network segment. A testbed with all three protocol stacks was operated for 45 days, and 18 multi-protocol and single-protocol attack scenarios were injected over a 10-day evaluation period. The learned linear combination, trained on a 5-day clean holdout with synthetic contamination, achieved the highest balanced accuracy (0.91) but required labelled data for weight estimation. The Dempster-Shafer rule achieved 0.88 without labelled data. The maximum rule performed consistently below 0.80. Results provide concrete guidance for operators designing multi-sensor detection pipelines.

SYN-PUB-10483.title: Protocol-Agnostic Anomaly Detection Using Byte-Level Feature Extraction from ICS Application Payloads
SYN-PUB-10483.text:
Protocol-Agnostic Anomaly Detection Using Byte-Level Feature Extraction from ICS Application Payloads (2026, journal, Journal of Industrial Network Security).
Authors: Jelena Kovačević (outside co-author); Péter Horváth (outside co-author); Krisztina Kiss (R1008); Milutin Paunović (R1022).
Keywords: protocol-agnostic; byte-level features; proprietary protocols; one-class SVM; heterogeneous ICS.
Most ICS anomaly detectors are designed for a specific protocol and rely on parsed field values. This paper investigates a protocol-agnostic approach in which raw application-layer payload bytes from the first 64 bytes of each PDU are used to construct feature vectors via byte-frequency histograms augmented with bigram entropy and mean absolute deviation of byte values. A one-class SVM and an Isolation Forest were trained on mixed-protocol captures from a testbed running Modbus, DNP3, and a proprietary vendor protocol for which no parser was available. The proprietary protocol represented 31% of traffic. Against seven attack scenarios including vendor-protocol-specific command injection, the protocol-agnostic detectors achieved AUROC values of 0.89 and 0.87 respectively, compared with 0.94 for a protocol-aware Modbus detector applied only to Modbus traffic. The paper discusses cases where protocol-agnostic features are sufficient and where parsed fields remain necessary, providing a decision framework for practitioners deploying detectors on heterogeneous industrial networks.

SYN-PUB-10523.title: Unsupervised anomaly detection on Modbus traffic
SYN-PUB-10523.text:
Unsupervised anomaly detection on Modbus traffic (2024, journal, Journal of Industrial Security).
Authors: Vuk Đukić (R1015); Milena Ostojić (outside co-author); Dragan Kovač (outside co-author).
Industrial control systems increasingly rely on Modbus, a legacy serial communication protocol widely deployed in manufacturing and critical infrastructure environments. Despite its prevalence, Modbus lacks built-in security mechanisms, making it highly susceptible to network-based attacks. This paper presents an unsupervised anomaly detection framework specifically designed for Modbus traffic analysis. The proposed approach leverages autoencoder-based neural networks trained exclusively on benign traffic to establish a baseline behavioural profile of legitimate industrial communications. Anomalies are identified by measuring reconstruction error against learned normal patterns, without requiring labelled attack data. The framework is evaluated on a synthetic dataset generated from a real-world programmable logic controller testbed, covering scenarios such as unauthorised function code injection, coil manipulation, and replay attacks. Experimental results demonstrate detection rates exceeding 94% across all attack categories, with a false positive rate below 2%. The paper also analyses the impact of traffic window size and encoding granularity on detection performance, offering practical guidance for deployment in resource-constrained industrial environments.

SYN-PUB-10525.title: A comparative study of intrusion detection architectures for SCADA networks
SYN-PUB-10525.text:
A comparative study of intrusion detection architectures for SCADA networks (2023, journal, IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics Security).
Authors: Milena Ostojić (outside co-author); Vuk Đukić (R1015); Nemanja Filipović (outside co-author).
Keywords: SCADA security; intrusion detection; industrial control systems; anomaly detection; network security.
Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) networks form the backbone of critical infrastructure sectors including energy distribution, water treatment, and transportation. Protecting these networks from cyber intrusions requires detection systems capable of operating on highly specialised industrial protocols while maintaining low false-positive rates in continuous operation. This paper conducts a systematic comparative evaluation of five intrusion detection architectures—signature-based, specification-based, statistical anomaly, deep learning, and hybrid approaches—applied to a common SCADA testbed. Each architecture is assessed across four attack categories: reconnaissance, command injection, man-in-the-middle, and denial-of-service. Performance is measured in terms of detection accuracy, latency, resource consumption, and adaptability to concept drift. Results show that hybrid architectures combining specification-based rules with neural anomaly scoring achieve the best overall balance, while purely deep-learning-based systems exhibit higher sensitivity to protocol version variability. The paper concludes with a decision framework to guide practitioners in selecting appropriate detection strategies based on operational constraints.

SYN-PUB-10531.title: Intrusion detection in resource-constrained IoT devices using lightweight recurrent models
SYN-PUB-10531.text:
Intrusion detection in resource-constrained IoT devices using lightweight recurrent models (2024, journal, IEEE Internet of Things Journal).
Authors: Vuk Đukić (R1015); Milena Ostojić (outside co-author); Rastko Mirković (outside co-author).
Keywords: IoT security; intrusion detection; recurrent neural networks; resource-constrained devices; anomaly detection.
Deploying intrusion detection directly on resource-constrained IoT devices such as microcontroller-based sensors and actuators presents fundamental challenges in terms of memory footprint, computational overhead, and energy consumption. This paper investigates the feasibility of implementing lightweight recurrent neural network models—specifically truncated LSTM and GRU variants—on devices with fewer than 256 KB of RAM. A model compression pipeline is developed that combines quantisation, pruning, and knowledge distillation to reduce model size by up to 94% relative to full-precision baselines, while preserving detection accuracy above 90% across standard IoT attack benchmarks. The compressed models are deployed on three representative IoT platforms and evaluated under realistic workload conditions. Power consumption measurements indicate that continuous on-device inference adds less than 4 mW overhead, making deployment feasible even on battery-powered nodes. The paper also proposes an adaptive inference strategy that dynamically reduces model complexity during high-load periods to prevent resource exhaustion. Results suggest that on-device intrusion detection is practically achievable for a broad class of constrained IoT deployments.

C018.title: DriveLogic Vojvodina d.o.o.
C018.text:
DriveLogic Vojvodina d.o.o. (C018): Automotive and mobility software, Novi Sad, 27 employees, founded 2004.
DriveLogic Vojvodina d.o.o. was founded in 2004 by Miroslav Vučić, a mechanical and electronics engineer who spent fifteen years at a German Tier-1 supplier, and his son Andrej Vučić, who joined after finishing his electrical engineering degree in Novi Sad. The two of them started with three workstations in a rented room and a single contract to port BSW modules for a mid-size European passenger car program. Twenty years later we are a team of twenty-seven engineers, all based in Novi Sad, and we have delivered software integration work on more than forty OEM projects. We focus entirely on AUTOSAR-based embedded software: configuration, integration, and V-cycle testing for powertrain, body and chassis ECUs. We do not build hardware, we do not sell IP, and we do not resell tools. Customers come to us because we do one thing and we do it carefully. Our engineers work directly inside the customer's development environment, using their toolchains and following their process rules. Our main customers are Tier-1 and Tier-2 suppliers delivering ECUs to European OEMs. We have worked with companies such as Hartfeld Automotive Systems (Germany), Rennova Electronics (Czech Republic) and Balkon Drive Solutions (Slovakia). Most contracts run between six and twenty-four months. What keeps customers coming back is straightforward: we document everything, we flag problems early, and we do not hide schedule risk.
Products: AUTOSAR Classic BSW configuration and software component integration; V-cycle test planning, execution and coverage reporting for ECU software; CAN, LIN and Ethernet communication stack integration and validation; ECU flashing, diagnostic tooling and UDS/OBD-II protocol support; AUTOSAR toolchain migration and legacy codebase porting.
Tech: AUTOSAR Classic (R4.x) and Vector DaVinci Configurator; CAPL scripting and CANoe/CANalyzer for network simulation and testing; TRACE32 and JTAG-based ECU debugging; Jenkins-based CI pipelines for build and static analysis; LDRA Testbed and gcov for branch and MC/DC coverage measurement; UDS (ISO 14229) and OBD-II (ISO 15031) diagnostic protocol implementation; Python scripting for test automation and report generation; MISRA-C:2012 compliance checking with PC-lint Plus.
Plans: DriveLogic Vojvodina plans to add a second delivery team by end of 2026 so we can run two large OEM projects in parallel without resource conflicts. We are also evaluating whether to extend our service scope to cover AUTOSAR Adaptive on high-performance compute platforms, which several of our existing customers are beginning to ask about.
R&D capacity: We can dedicate one senior engineer part-time (roughly 40% of their working week) to a collaborative development or research activity, provided it is directly tied to tools or methods we will use in active projects.
Past collaborations: We worked informally with a controls research group at a technical institute in Subotica around 2019 on a model-based calibration study, but the output was not published and there was no formal agreement.

R0948.title: Mirjana Vidaković
R0948.text:
Mirjana Vidaković (R0948): Full Professor, Department of Computing and Control Engineering, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Model-Driven Engineering; Embedded Systems Software; Software Architecture; Automotive Software Engineering.
Keywords: AUTOSAR; model-driven engineering; metamodel transformation; code generation; ARXML; domain-specific language; template-based synthesis; Eclipse Modeling Framework; real-time embedded systems; toolchain integration.
Bio: Mirjana Vidaković received her Dipl.Ing. degree in computer engineering from the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad in 2001, her M.Sc. in 2005, and her Ph.D. in 2011, with a dissertation on metamodel-driven generation of AUTOSAR software component descriptors. She joined the Department of Computing and Control Engineering as an assistant professor in 2012 and was promoted to full professor in 2022. Her research group focuses on model-driven engineering (MDE) for safety-relevant embedded systems, with particular emphasis on AUTOSAR-compliant architectures, ARXML artefact manipulation, template-based code synthesis, and toolchain integration. She teaches courses on embedded systems software, domain-specific languages, and software architectures for real-time systems. The group uses Eclipse Modeling Framework, Ecore-based metamodeling tools, AUTOSAR authoring environments, and hardware-in-the-loop test benches available in the Faculty's Embedded Systems Laboratory.
Open to: joint projects with companies on AUTOSAR toolchain development or customisation; contract research on ARXML artefact processing and model transformation; industrial PhD supervision for candidates from automotive or embedded-software companies; student internships in the Embedded Systems Laboratory; consulting on MDE toolchain architecture and AUTOSAR workflow design.
Industry experience: Vidaković has served as a technical consultant to Embron d.o.o., a Novi Sad-based embedded-software company, on AUTOSAR toolchain architecture over three separate engagements between 2015 and 2022. She also participated in a four-month knowledge-transfer engagement with a regional automotive Tier-1 supplier in 2018 focused on introducing MDE practices into their ECU development workflow.
Notes: Vidaković is currently supervising three doctoral students, which limits capacity for new long-term commitments before mid-2026. She has expressed preference for collaborations that involve access to realistic industrial AUTOSAR model corpora, as the Faculty's internal model library covers only a narrow range of ECU domains. Short-term consulting or focused contract research engagements are feasible at any time.

C018-CH1.title: We manually generate around 3,200 AUTOSAR software component configuration files per project and it takes two engineers three weeks; one of our competitors apparently automated this and turned around the same job in four days — at current rates we are losing bids on price.
C018-CH1.text:
We manually generate around 3,200 AUTOSAR software component configuration files per project and it takes two engineers three weeks; one of our competitors apparently automated this and turned around the same job in four days — at current rates we are losing bids on price.

Every new project hands us a System Extract from the customer and we then have to produce AUTOSAR SWC configuration files — port definitions, inter-runnable variables, timing constraints, the lot — by hand inside DaVinci Configurator. On the last two projects we counted roughly 3,200 files each time. Two senior engineers spend three weeks doing nothing else. We have tried building Excel-based templates to speed up the repetitive parts, and that helped a little, but the real problem is that the mapping logic between the System Extract and the final ARXML is still done by a person reading a document and typing. We heard from a contact at a Romanian company that they built something — probably a script or a generator layer on top of the tool API — that brings the same volume of work down to four days. We do not know the details. We have the DaVinci API documentation and we have two engineers who write Python, but nobody has had time to build the tooling properly. We are losing price-sensitive bids. A good outcome is a generation process that gets us from a clean System Extract to a reviewable first-draft configuration set in under one working day, with engineers only doing review and exception handling.

SYN-PUB-09982.title: Toolchain-Independent Representation of AUTOSAR Timing Constraints Using a Standardised Metamodel
SYN-PUB-09982.text:
Toolchain-Independent Representation of AUTOSAR Timing Constraints Using a Standardised Metamodel (2025, journal, Embedded Systems Letters).
Authors: Dragan Luković (outside co-author); Tomáš Bureš (outside co-author); Milena Stanković (outside co-author); Mirjana Vidaković (R0948).
Keywords: AUTOSAR TIMEX; timing constraints; metamodel interoperability; model exchange; Acceleo.
Timing constraint specifications in AUTOSAR are expressed through the Timing Extensions (TIMEX) sub-schema, but the way authoring tools serialise TIMEX artefacts varies substantially, causing interoperability problems when exchanging models between organisations using different tools. This paper proposes a standardised intermediate metamodel for AUTOSAR timing constraints covering end-to-end latency constraints, synchronisation constraints, age constraints, and execution time annotations. Import adaptors were implemented for three commercial AUTOSAR authoring environments and validated on a set of 17 timing specifications of varying complexity collected from two automotive projects. The metamodel-normalised representations enabled automated comparison of semantically equivalent constraints authored in different tools; comparison detected four constraint semantics discrepancies that had gone unnoticed during manual review. An Acceleo-based exporter regenerates tool-specific ARXML from the normalised metamodel with measured round-trip fidelity of 98.6% across all constraint types.

SYN-PUB-03795.title: Domain-Specific Language for Configuring AUTOSAR Communication Matrices
SYN-PUB-03795.text:
Domain-Specific Language for Configuring AUTOSAR Communication Matrices (2016, conference, Proceedings of the Workshop on Model-Driven Engineering for Embedded Systems).
Authors: Borislav Đorđević (outside co-author); Vukica Grujić (R0305); Andrea Mocci (outside co-author); Strahinja Radović (R0385); Mirjana Vidaković (R0948).
Keywords: DSL; Xtext; Xtend; communication matrix; AUTOSAR 4.2.
Communication matrix configuration in AUTOSAR involves mapping signals to PDUs, defining timing parameters, and assigning network identifiers, all expressed in verbose ARXML. This paper presents ComMatDSL, a textual domain-specific language designed to express communication matrix configurations concisely. The language was defined using Xtext and includes a type system aligned with AUTOSAR data types. A model-to-ARXML generator was implemented using Xtend. The language was evaluated with five engineers from a regional embedded-software consultancy, each of whom configured three bus networks of increasing complexity. Compared to direct ARXML editing, ComMatDSL configurations were on average 76% shorter in character count and contained 58% fewer syntactic errors in the first-draft stage. A round-trip test on 22 reference matrices confirmed semantic equivalence of the generated ARXML with manually authored originals. The DSL is available as an Eclipse feature and targets AUTOSAR 4.2.

SYN-PUB-09979.title: A Transformation Chain for Migrating AUTOSAR Classic SWC Models to Adaptive Platform Service Skeletons
SYN-PUB-09979.text:
A Transformation Chain for Migrating AUTOSAR Classic SWC Models to Adaptive Platform Service Skeletons (2022, conference, Proceedings of the European Conference on Software Architecture and Component Engineering).
Authors: Borislav Đorđević (outside co-author); Marco Gennari (outside co-author); Ján Kolář (outside co-author); Mirjana Vidaković (R0948).
Keywords: migration; AUTOSAR Classic; AUTOSAR Adaptive; transformation chain; service skeleton.
Migration from AUTOSAR Classic to Adaptive Platform is increasingly relevant as vehicle architectures shift toward high-performance compute nodes. This paper describes a three-step transformation chain that takes Classic SWC descriptions in ARXML 4.3 as input and produces Adaptive Platform service skeleton headers and SIMs conforming to AP 21.11. The first transformation normalises Classic port interfaces into a platform-independent intermediate model; the second maps the intermediate model to AP service interface definitions; the third generates C++ skeleton headers using Acceleo. Migration was applied to 38 SWCs from two body-domain ECU projects. Thirty-one SWCs migrated fully automatically; seven required manual completion of data type mappings that have no direct AP equivalent. The paper analyses the seven exceptions and proposes three extension points in the intermediate metamodel that would reduce manual effort in future migrations. Compilation of generated skeletons succeeded on an AP reference implementation without modifications.

SYN-PRJ-0432.title: Model-Driven Engineering Methods for Verified Automotive Embedded Software
SYN-PRJ-0432.text:
MDEVS: Model-Driven Engineering Methods for Verified Automotive Embedded Software (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2021–2024).
Participants: R0948 principal investigator; R0054 team member.
Partners: Faculty of Electronic Engineering, University of Niš; Slovak University of Technology in Bratislava; Embron d.o.o., Novi Sad.
The project investigates formal and semi-formal methods for verifying the correctness of model transformations used in AUTOSAR toolchains. Activities include: formalising ATL transformation semantics in a subset of Z notation, developing a property-based test generation framework for Ecore-based transformations, and building a prototype transformation verification tool integrated into the Eclipse ecosystem. The project collaborates with the Faculty of Electronic Engineering in Niš and the Slovak University of Technology in Bratislava. Industrial relevance is maintained through a liaison with a regional embedded-software consultancy that provides representative AUTOSAR model corpora for evaluation. The project supports two doctoral students and targets six journal publications over its four-year duration.

SYN-PUB-09973.title: Metamodel Definition for AUTOSAR Software Component Descriptors Using Ecore
SYN-PUB-09973.text:
Metamodel Definition for AUTOSAR Software Component Descriptors Using Ecore (2010, journal, International Journal of Embedded and Real-Time Communication Systems).
Authors: Dragan Luković (outside co-author); Predrag Rakić (outside co-author); Mirjana Vidaković (R0948).
Keywords: Ecore metamodel; AUTOSAR SWC; ARXML; ATL transformation; Eclipse Modeling Framework.
This paper presents a structured approach to defining an Ecore-based metamodel that captures the structural semantics of AUTOSAR software component (SWC) descriptors as specified in the AUTOSAR 3.2 standard. The metamodel covers port interfaces, runnables, inter-runnable variables, and timing constraints. Conformance was verified by instantiating 14 SWC types taken from a reference body-control-module specification and checking instance validity against the AUTOSAR schema. The metamodel was implemented as an Eclipse plug-in and exposed a tree-based editor. Transformation experiments using ATL showed that round-trip consistency between the Ecore model and hand-authored ARXML could be maintained with fewer than 0.3% structural deviations across 430 tested descriptors. The contribution is a reusable metamodel layer that decouples SWC authoring from the verbose ARXML syntax and enables downstream model-to-text generation without direct schema manipulation.

SYN-PUB-09978.title: Model-Driven Engineering for Automotive Embedded Software: A Practitioner's Guide
SYN-PUB-09978.text:
Model-Driven Engineering for Automotive Embedded Software: A Practitioner's Guide (2020, book chapter, Advances in Embedded and Cyber-Physical Systems (edited volume, Springer Verlag Balkans)).
Authors: Dragan Luković (outside co-author); Mirjana Vidaković (R0948).
Keywords: MDE practice; AUTOSAR; toolchain; ATL; transformation testing.
This book chapter provides a structured treatment of MDE practice as applied to automotive embedded software, with AUTOSAR as the primary platform. It covers the spectrum from metamodel definition through transformation authoring to final artefact generation, and situates each activity within a typical automotive development V-model. The chapter draws on case material from three ECU development projects to illustrate how metamodel granularity choices affect toolchain complexity and traceability. It includes a worked example of a complete SWC-to-C code generation pipeline using Ecore, ATL, and Acceleo, with all intermediate artefacts described in detail. A section on toolchain validation discusses coverage criteria for transformation testing and introduces a mutation-based adequacy measure adapted to ATL rules. Intended for software engineers entering the automotive domain and for academics setting up MDE courses with industrial relevance.

SYN-PUB-06834.title: Consistency Checking Between ARXML System Descriptions and Deployment Configurations
SYN-PUB-06834.text:
Consistency Checking Between ARXML System Descriptions and Deployment Configurations (2013, conference, Softversko Inženjerstvo i Primenjene Tehnologije (SIPAT)).
Authors: Borislav Đorđević (outside co-author); Nenad Dimitrijević (R0592); Luka Knežević (R0802); Nikola Sremčević (outside co-author); Mirjana Vidaković (R0948).
Keywords: ARXML; OCL constraints; consistency checking; AUTOSAR deployment; Eclipse plug-in.
AUTOSAR system descriptions and their corresponding deployment configurations are maintained as separate ARXML files and can diverge during iterative development. This paper describes a rule-based consistency checker implemented as an Eclipse plug-in that operates on a merged in-memory model assembled from multiple ARXML artefacts. Forty-three consistency rules derived from the AUTOSAR 4.1 specification were encoded as OCL constraints. The checker was applied to six industrial-style test configurations provided by a regional automotive supplier, ranging from 12 to 78 ECUs per configuration. It detected an average of 8.4 rule violations per configuration that were not flagged by the supplier's existing tooling, most relating to signal mapping mismatches and unresolved component prototype references. False positive rate was 2.1% after a calibration phase involving two domain experts. The tool reduced manual configuration review time by approximately 40% in a two-week pilot.

SYN-PUB-09974.title: Template-Based Generation of AUTOSAR RTE Stubs from Port Interface Models
SYN-PUB-09974.text:
Template-Based Generation of AUTOSAR RTE Stubs from Port Interface Models (2012, conference, Proceedings of the Eastern European Conference on Embedded Systems).
Authors: Mirjana Vidaković (R0948); Predrag Rakić (outside co-author); Tomáš Bureš (outside co-author).
Keywords: Xpand; RTE stub; AUTOSAR Classic; model-to-text; MISRA-C.
Runtime Environment (RTE) stub generation is a recurring manual effort in AUTOSAR development workflows. This work describes a model-to-text pipeline in which Xpand templates consume an Ecore-based port-interface model and produce syntactically correct RTE stub files for AUTOSAR Classic Platform 4.0. The pipeline was evaluated on three representative Electronic Control Unit (ECU) designs—a door-control unit, a seat-adjustment module, and a battery-management interface—together comprising 67 port interfaces and 112 runnables. Generation time averaged 1.4 seconds per ECU on a standard workstation. Generated stubs were compiled without modification using a commercial compiler suite and passed static analysis with no MISRA-C:2004 violations in 94% of cases; the remaining 6% required minor pointer-cast annotations. Manual effort for stub authoring was reduced from approximately four person-hours to under fifteen minutes per ECU, as measured in a controlled comparison with two experienced engineers.

W4394692031.title: Automated Mapping of Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures to MITRE ATT&CK Tactics
W4394692031.text: Information, 2024. Effectively understanding and categorizing vulnerabilities is vital in the ever-evolving cybersecurity landscape, since only one exposure can have a devastating effect on the entire system. Given the increasingly massive number of threats and the size of modern infrastructures, the need for structured, uniform cybersecurity knowledge systems arose. To tackle this challenge, the MITRE Corporation set up two powerful sources of cyber threat and vulnerability information, namely the Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) list focused on identifying and fixing software vulnerabilities, and the MITRE ATT&CK Enterprise Matrix, which is a framework for defining and categorizing adversary actions and ways to defend against them. At the moment, the two are not directly linked, even if such a link would have a significant positive impact on the cybersecurity community. This study aims to automatically map CVEs to the corresponding 14 MITRE ATT&CK tactics using state-of-the-art transformer-based models. Various architectures, from encoders to generative large-scale models, are employed to tackle this multilabel classification problem. Our results are promising, with a SecRoBERTa model performing best with an F1 score of 77.81%, which is closely followed by SecBERT (78.77%), CyBERT (78.54%), and TARS (78.01%), while GPT-4 showed a weak performance in zero-shot settings (22.04%). …

W4389608980.title: Change Point Detection with Adaptive Measurement Schedules for Network Performance Verification
W4389608980.text: Proceedings of the ACM on Measurement and Analysis of Computing Systems, 2023. When verifying that a communications network fulfills its specified performance, it is critical to note sudden shifts in network behavior as quickly as possible. Change point detection methods can be useful in this endeavor, but classical methods rely on measuring with a fixed measurement period, which can often be suboptimal in terms of measurement costs. In this paper, we extend the existing framework of change point detection with a notion of physical time. Instead of merely deciding when to stop, agents must now also decide at which future time to take the next measurement. Agents must now minimize the necessary number of measurements pre- and post-change, while maintaining a trade-off between post-change delay and false alarm rate. We establish, through this framework, the suboptimality of typical periodic measurements and propose a simple alternative, called crisis mode agents. We show analytically that crisis mode agents significantly outperform periodic measurements schemes. We further verify this in numerical evaluation, both on an array of synthetic change point detection problems as well as on the problem of detecting traffic load changes in a 5G test bed through end-to-end RTT measurements.

SYN-PUB-06548.title: Mapping IPv6 Attack Surfaces: Challenges for Existing Agent-Based Scanners
SYN-PUB-06548.text:
Mapping IPv6 Attack Surfaces: Challenges for Existing Agent-Based Scanners (2020, journal, Journal of Network and Systems Engineering).
Authors: Andreja Ilić (outside co-author); Borivoj Stanković (outside co-author); Árpád Nagy (R0564).
Keywords: IPv6; host discovery; NDP; agent-based scanning; attack surface.
IPv6's vastly larger address space makes exhaustive address-space scanning computationally infeasible, requiring fundamentally different approaches to host discovery than those used in IPv4 environments. This paper systematically evaluates six agent-based scanning architectures against dual-stack and IPv6-only testbeds of 150 hosts and analyses their host-discovery rates, false-positive counts, and scan durations. Results show that methods relying on direct address-range sweeping achieve under 12% discovery on pure IPv6 segments compared to 97% on equivalent IPv4 segments. Neighbour Discovery Protocol exploitation, DNS reverse-zone enumeration, and passive traffic observation are assessed as alternatives, with the DNS-based method achieving 78% discovery on correctly configured networks. The paper derives a prioritised pipeline combining these sources and demonstrates its integration into an existing multi-agent scanning framework, raising combined discovery to 89%.

SYN-PUB-06550.title: Temporal Dynamics of Attack Graphs: Modelling Vulnerability Disclosure and Patch Lag
SYN-PUB-06550.text:
Temporal Dynamics of Attack Graphs: Modelling Vulnerability Disclosure and Patch Lag (2024, journal, Journal of Computer Security and Privacy).
Authors: Orsolya Molnár (outside co-author); Nikola Vujović (outside co-author); Árpád Nagy (R0564).
Keywords: temporal attack graph; patch lag; CVE lifecycle; vulnerability disclosure; network security.
Attack graphs are typically computed as static snapshots, but the real vulnerability state of a network changes continuously as new CVEs are disclosed and patches are applied at varying rates across different asset classes. This paper introduces a temporal attack graph model in which vulnerability nodes carry activation and deactivation timestamps derived from NVD disclosure dates and patch deployment logs collected from a university IT infrastructure over a 36-month observation window. The dataset covers 214 unique hosts and 1,102 distinct CVE occurrences. Analysis of the resulting temporal sequence of graphs shows that the median window of exploitability for a newly disclosed critical vulnerability on an unpatched host is 23 days. The model is used to retrospectively identify four periods during which critical exploit paths existed that would not have appeared in any single static snapshot, underscoring the limitations of periodic scanning alone.

W2883401192.title: An Efficient ECG Lossless Compression System for Embedded Platforms With Telemedicine Applications
W2883401192.text: IEEE Access, 2018. This paper presents a method for wireless ECG compression and zero lossless decompression using a combination of three different techniques in order to increase storage space while reducing transmission time. The first technique used in the proposed algorithm is an adaptive linear prediction; it achieves high sensitivity and positive prediction. The second technique is content-adaptive Golomb-Rice coding, used with a window size to encode the residual of prediction error. The third technique is the use of a suitable packing format; this enables the real-time decoding process. The proposed algorithm is evaluated and verified using over 48 recordings from the MIT-BIH arrhythmia database, and it shown to be able to achieve a lossless bit compression rate of 2.83× in Lead V1 and 2.77× in Lead V2. The proposed algorithm shows better performance results in comparison to previous lossless ECG compression studies in real time; it can be used in data transmission methods for superior biomedical signals for bounded bandwidth across e-health devices. The overall compression system is also built with an ARM M4 processor, which ensures high accuracy performance and consistent results in the timing operation of the system.

R0905.title: Filip Mijatović
R0905.text:
Filip Mijatović (R0905): Assistant Professor, Department of Power, Electronics and Telecommunications, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Microelectronics and mixed-signal circuit design; Wireless sensor networks and embedded systems; Biomedical instrumentation; Low-power communication protocols.
Keywords: ultra-low-power design; body-area networks; mixed-signal CMOS; biopotential acquisition; duty-cycled MAC; energy harvesting; sub-threshold circuits; wireless health monitoring; impedance spectroscopy; biomedical sampling constraints.
Bio: Filip Mijatović received his B.Sc. and M.Sc. degrees in Electronics and Telecommunications from the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, in 2009 and 2012 respectively, and his Ph.D. from the same institution in 2018, with a thesis on duty-cycled MAC protocols for implantable sensor nodes. W4392173026.title: A Low-Noise Low-Power 0.001Hz–1kHz Neural Recording System-on-Chip With Sample-Level Duty-Cycling
W4392173026.text: IEEE Transactions on Biomedical Circuits and Systems, 2024. Advances in brain-machine interfaces and wearable biomedical sensors for healthcare and human-computer interactions call for precision electrophysiology to resolve a variety of biopotential signals across the body that cover a wide range of frequencies, from the mHz-range electrogastrogram (EGG) to the kHz-range electroneurogram (ENG). Existing integrated wearable solutions for minimally invasive biopotential recordings are limited in detection range and accuracy due to trade-offs in bandwidth, noise, input impedance, and power consumption. This article presents a 16-channel wide-band ultra-low-noise neural recording system-on-chip (SoC) fabricated in 65nm CMOS for chronic use in mobile healthcare settings that spans a bandwidth of 0.001 Hz to 1 kHz through a featured sample-level duty-cycling (SLDC) mode. Each recording channel is implemented by a delta-sigma analog-to-digital converter (ADC) achieving 1.0$\mu$V${}_{rms}$input-referred noise over 1Hz–1kHz bandwidth with a Noise Efficiency Factor (NEF) of 2.93 in continuous operation mode. In SLDC mode, the power supply is duty-cycled while maintaining consistently low input-referred noise levels at ultra-low frequencies (1.1$\mu$V${}_{rms}$over 0.001Hz–1Hz) and 435 M$\Omega$input impedance. …

SYN-PUB-09632.title: Duty-cycled MAC scheduling with deadline-aware slot allocation for implantable sensor nodes
SYN-PUB-09632.text:
Duty-cycled MAC scheduling with deadline-aware slot allocation for implantable sensor nodes (2018, journal, IEEE Transactions on Biomedical Circuits and Systems).
Authors: Filip Mijatović (R0905); Dragan Vuković (outside co-author); Christoph Brandner (outside co-author).
Keywords: MAC scheduling; deadline-aware; duty cycling; implantable sensor; IEEE 802.15.4.
This work, developed as part of the author's doctoral research, proposes a beacon-enabled superframe structure derived from IEEE 802.15.4 in which guaranteed time slots are assigned according to each sensor stream's sampling deadline rather than priority class alone. The scheduler runs on a body hub modelled as a 32-bit ARM Cortex-M3 at 4 MHz and accepts registration messages carrying a sampling period, payload size, and maximum tolerable latency for each node. A first-fit decreasing bin-packing heuristic assigns contiguous slots within each superframe. Simulation across 10,000 randomly generated workloads with 2–8 nodes showed that deadline miss rates remained below 0.3% for workloads at up to 80% superframe utilisation. Radio duty cycle for a six-node ECG plus EMG scenario was reduced to 1.8% compared with 6.4% under a fixed-slot baseline, yielding a projected 3.5-fold increase in node battery lifetime. The protocol was prototyped on a Cortex-M0 hub with four slave nodes and validated against simulated data.

SYN-PUB-09631.title: Energy budget analysis of implantable glucose monitors: from sensing front-end to RF uplink
SYN-PUB-09631.text:
Energy budget analysis of implantable glucose monitors: from sensing front-end to RF uplink (2017, journal, Journal of Medical Engineering and Instrumentation).
Authors: Filip Mijatović (R0905); Nataša Ristić (outside co-author); Miroslav Petrović (outside co-author).
Keywords: implantable glucose monitor; amperometric potentiostat; energy budget; OOK transmitter; duty cycling.
Continuous glucose monitors intended for subcutaneous implantation face a hard energy ceiling imposed by the volume available for primary cells or inductive charging coils. This work presents a structured energy budget partitioning the 50 µW mean power allocated in a hypothetical 1 cm³ implant across four subsystems: the amperometric sensing front-end (8 µW), the 8-bit ADC (3 µW), the microcontroller running a linearisation algorithm (12 µW), and the 2.4 GHz OOK transmitter (27 µW active, duty-cycled to 0.4%). A custom switched-capacitor potentiostat operating at 100 mV applied potential consumed 6.1 µW measured on bench. The ADC was a successive-approximation design clocked at 10 kHz with an effective number of bits of 7.6. End-to-end system simulation using measured component data predicted a node lifetime of 14 days from a 4 mAh primary lithium cell, which is consistent with reported values in the literature for comparable implant geometries. Identified bottlenecks and proposed architectural changes are discussed.

C001/website/2024-01-15/What We Do — Arm.title: What We Do — ArmaturaSec d.o.o.
C001/website/2024-01-15/What We Do — Arm.text: ArmaturaSec builds network security appliances for operational technology environments. If you run a water treatment plant, an electricity distribution substation, or a manufacturing line and you need to control who can talk to your PLCs and whether that traffic looks legitimate, that is what our products are designed for. We are not a general-purpose cybersecurity company. We do not sell endpoint agents, email filters, or cloud security platforms. Every product we have shipped since 2008 has been a hardware device that sits inside an industrial network and inspects or controls traffic at the protocol level. Our NetGuard-OT appliance handles network access control: it enforces rules about which devices can communicate, blocks unauthorised connections, and logs everything in a format that your existing SCADA historian can ingest. The Mini variant fits on a standard DIN rail for installations where cabinet space is limited. ProtoSense is our protocol inspection module. It understands Modbus TCP and BACnet/IP at the message level, not just the packet level, so it can tell you that a device sent a write command to a coil it has never written to before — not just that traffic occurred. Our SecAudit service is a one-time on-site engagement. Two of our engineers spend two days on your site, map the network as it actually exists, identify the gaps between that and how it is supposed to be configured, and produce a written report with prioritised findings. We work with clients in Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, and Montenegro. Most of our installations are in the energy and water sectors. A growing share are in food and beverage manufacturing. If you want to talk about a specific installation or you have a question about whether our products fit your environment, contact our sales team in Zrenjanin.

W4224248050.title: Lightweight Long Short-Term Memory Variational Auto-Encoder for Multivariate Time Series Anomaly Detection in Industrial Control Systems
W4224248050.text: Sensors, 2022. Heterogeneous cyberattacks against industrial control systems (ICSs) have had a strong impact on the physical world in recent decades. Connecting devices to the internet enables new attack surfaces for attackers. The intrusion of ICSs, such as the manipulation of industrial sensory or actuator data, can be the cause for anomalous ICS behaviors. This poses a threat to the infrastructure that is critical for the operation of a modern city. Nowadays, the best techniques for detecting anomalies in ICSs are based on machine learning and, more recently, deep learning. Cybersecurity in ICSs is still an emerging field, and industrial datasets that can be used to develop anomaly detection techniques are rare. In this paper, we propose an unsupervised deep learning methodology for anomaly detection in ICSs, specifically, a lightweight long short-term memory variational auto-encoder (LW-LSTM-VAE) architecture. We successfully demonstrate our solution under two ICS applications, namely, water purification and water distribution plants. Our proposed method proves to be efficient in detecting anomalies in these applications and improves upon reconstruction-based anomaly detection methods presented in previous work. For example, we successfully detected 82.16% of the anomalies in the scenario of the widely used Secure Water Treatment (SWaT) benchmark. The deep learning architecture we propose has the added advantage of being extremely lightweight.

SYN-PUB-10478.title: Evaluating the Effect of Protocol Encryption on Traffic-Based Anomaly Detection: OPC UA Security Mode Comparison
SYN-PUB-10478.text:
Evaluating the Effect of Protocol Encryption on Traffic-Based Anomaly Detection: OPC UA Security Mode Comparison (2019, conference, Proceedings of the Central European Workshop on Industrial Communication Security (CEWICS)).
Authors: Tibor Farkas (outside co-author); Marek Novotný (outside co-author); Krisztina Kiss (R1008).
Keywords: OPC UA; encryption; traffic features; one-class SVM; security mode.
OPC UA supports three security modes—None, Sign, and SignAndEncrypt—and this paper evaluates how each mode affects the discriminability of traffic features used in unsupervised anomaly detectors. Experiments were conducted on a testbed comprising an OPC UA server, two client applications, and an embedded data historian. Seventeen traffic features extractable from unencrypted traffic were assessed for their availability under Sign and SignAndEncrypt modes using packet capture before and after the application layer. Under SignAndEncrypt, 11 of 17 features became unavailable or uninformative at the packet level; however, timing, packet length distribution, and session-level handshake frequency remained discriminative. A reduced 6-feature one-class SVM trained on these surviving features achieved a detection rate of 0.83 against four attack scenarios, compared with 0.91 for the full 17-feature detector on unencrypted traffic. The paper discusses the implications for passive inline monitoring architectures and proposes a broker-based decryption approach for trusted network segments.

SYN-PUB-10472.title: Statistical Baseline Modelling of Modbus/TCP Traffic in a Substation Automation Network
SYN-PUB-10472.text:
Statistical Baseline Modelling of Modbus/TCP Traffic in a Substation Automation Network (2010, journal, Journal of Industrial Network Security).
Authors: Goran Milošević (outside co-author); Tibor Farkas (outside co-author); Krisztina Kiss (R1008).
Keywords: Modbus/TCP; statistical baseline; Mahalanobis distance; substation automation; one-class detection.
This paper describes the construction of per-register statistical baselines for Modbus/TCP traffic captured over six months on a live substation automation testbed. For each register address, empirical distributions of inter-request intervals, payload values, and function code sequences were estimated using kernel density estimation with a Gaussian kernel and bandwidth selected by cross-validation. A one-class detector based on Mahalanobis distance thresholding over a 20-feature vector was evaluated against 14 manually injected attack scenarios, including replay, coil-write injection, and scan sweeps. At a false positive rate of 0.5%, the detector achieved a true positive rate of 91.4% across all attack types. The paper also quantifies the effect of seasonal load variation on baseline drift and proposes a sliding-window recalibration schedule with a 72-hour update period that maintains detection performance without human intervention. Results are compared with a fixed-threshold rule-based baseline, which achieved 67% TPR at the same FPR. The testbed comprised three Siemens-compatible PLCs connected over a deterministic switched Ethernet fabric.

W4391996970.title: Unsupervised Learning Approach for Anomaly Detection in Industrial Control Systems
W4391996970.text: Applied System Innovation, 2024. Industrial control systems (ICSs) play a crucial role in managing and monitoring critical processes across various industries, such as manufacturing, energy, and water treatment. The connection of equipment from various manufacturers, complex communication methods, and the need for the continuity of operations in a limited environment make it difficult to detect system anomalies. Traditional approaches that rely on supervised machine learning require time and expertise due to the need for labeled datasets. This study suggests an alternative approach to identifying anomalous behavior within ICSs by means of unsupervised machine learning. The approach employs unsupervised machine learning to identify anomalous behavior within ICSs. This study shows that unsupervised learning algorithms can effectively detect and classify anomalous behavior without the need for pre-labeled data using a composite autoencoder model. Based on a dataset that utilizes HIL-augmented ICSs (HAIs), this study shows that the model is capable of accurately identifying important data characteristics and detecting anomalous patterns related to both value and time. Intentional error data injection experiments could potentially be used to validate the model’s robustness in real-time monitoring and industrial process performance optimization. As a result, this approach can improve system reliability and operational efficiency, which can establish a foundation for safe and sustainable ICS operations.

W3006480895.title: Unsupervised Anomaly Detection for Network Data Streams in Industrial Control Systems
W3006480895.text: Information, 2020. The development and integration of information technology and industrial control networks have expanded the magnitude of new data; detecting anomalies or discovering other valid information from them is of vital importance to the stable operation of industrial control systems. This paper proposes an incremental unsupervised anomaly detection method that can quickly analyze and process large-scale real-time data. Our evaluation on the Secure Water Treatment dataset shows that the method is converging to its offline counterpart for infinitely growing data streams.

SYN-PUB-00722.title: Detecting Stealthy Coil-Write Injection in Modbus Networks Using Temporal Autoencoder Ensembles
SYN-PUB-00722.text:
Detecting Stealthy Coil-Write Injection in Modbus Networks Using Temporal Autoencoder Ensembles (2023, journal, IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics).
Authors: Mirjana Stošić (outside co-author); Veljko Pantelić (R0995); Marek Novotný (outside co-author); Krisztina Kiss (R1008); Nina Dimitrijević (R0054).
Keywords: stealthy attacks; autoencoder ensemble; coil-write injection; Modbus; temporal features.
Stealthy coil-write injection attacks modify a small number of PLC output coils at irregular intervals designed to evade detectors sensitive only to rate or volume changes. This paper evaluates temporal autoencoder ensembles—ten autoencoders trained on temporally shuffled subsets of a 60-day Modbus/TCP capture—for detecting such attacks. Each autoencoder receives a 30-dimensional feature vector derived from 5-second windows including coil change frequency, write-to-read ratio per coil address, and inter-write interval statistics. Anomaly scores from ensemble members are aggregated by the maximum rule. Against 240 injected stealthy attack episodes of varying intensity (1 to 8 modified coils per window), the ensemble achieved recall of 0.89 at a false positive rate of 0.8 per hour, compared with 0.64 for a single autoencoder and 0.58 for a static threshold detector. Computational cost of the ensemble was 2.3× that of a single autoencoder, remaining feasible on edge hardware.
